h1: The 9 Best Monitor Light Bars for Gaming of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Gaming Monitor Light Bars: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 9 monitor light bars for gaming compared on bias lighting, RGB, curved-screen fit and controls, from BenQ to Govee and Razer.
summary: The BenQ ScreenBar Halo 2 is the best light bar for gaming in a dark room: independent front and back lighting, a wireless dial and a motion sensor. For a lit desk without glare on a budget, the Quntis PRO+ adds 1200 lux and a remote. The Govee G1 is the only one that syncs its backlight to what is on screen. Razer's Aether is for Chroma ecosystem users, and the Quntis Curved RGB is built for curved panels.
intro: A gaming light bar does two jobs that people mix up. A front light puts light on your desk and keyboard without bouncing off the screen. A backlight casts a glow on the wall behind the monitor, which cuts the contrast between a bright panel and a dark room. Few bars do both well, and the best choice depends on which problem you actually have.

We reviewed nine bars on paper, from plain desk lamps to RGB and screen-sync models. Ranking starts with how well each handles both jobs, then curved-monitor fit, controls and ecosystem integration. Cheaper bars are good at the first job and limited at the second.

products.name: BenQ ScreenBar Halo 2, Backlight, Wireless Dial, Motion Sensor
products.verdict: Independent front and back lighting with a wireless dial and motion sensor.
products.description:
The Halo 2 combines a front desk light with a backlight on the rear, each with its own brightness control. It powers over USB-C, includes a wireless dial and a motion sensor, lists CRI 95 and fits curved monitors from 1000R to 1800R.

It wins because it does both jobs in one bar: it lights the desk and softens the glow behind the screen, which is what reduces eye strain in a dark gaming room. Quntis models match it on front light, but few handle the backlight this cleanly.

Buy it for a dark room. The caveat is that its backlight is a white-light bias effect, not a color show.

products.name: Quntis Monitor Light Bar PRO+, 20-inch, Remote, 1200 Lux
products.verdict: A 20 inch bar with 1200 lux, auto-dimming and a wireless remote.
products.description:
Quntis PRO+ is a 20 inch bar with a wireless remote, auto-dimming and 1200 lux, the highest output in the Quntis lineup. It lists CRI 95 and is compatible with curved monitors.

It ranks second because it handles the first job best: bright, glare-free desk light, and the length covers ultrawides. It has no backlight, which is what the BenQ adds.

Best for an ultrawide desk. The caveat is that there is no rear glow.
products.idealFor: Ultrawide desks that need bright light.

products.name: Govee Gaming Light for Monitor G1, RGBIC LED, Screen Color Sync
products.verdict: The only pick that syncs backlight color to the screen, with 123 scenes.
products.description:
Govee's G1 uses RGBIC LEDs with screen color sync, 123 scene modes, music sync and app control, and is built for 27 to 34 inch monitors.

It ranks third because screen color sync is unique here: the rear glow follows what is on screen. It is a backlight, not a desk light, so it does not replace a front bar.

Best for immersive gaming. The caveat is that it does not light your desk.
products.skipIf: You want to light your desk.

products.name: Razer Aether Monitor LED Light Bar, Chroma RGB, Front and Back
products.verdict: Chroma RGB with front and back lighting and Razer Synapse integration.
products.description:
Razer's Aether lists Chroma RGB with 16.8 million colors, front and back lighting, Alexa compatibility, Razer Synapse integration and the Razer Gamer Room app.

It ranks fourth because it offers both front and back light like the BenQ, with ecosystem integration, but the value is highest for owners of other Razer gear.

Best for Razer fans. The caveat is that the integration matters little if you have no Razer gear.

products.name: BenQ ScreenBar Pro, Motion Sensor, USB-C, 1000 Lux
products.verdict: 1000 lux, an ultrasonic motion sensor and a wireless dial, powered by USB-C.
products.description:
ScreenBar Pro lists an ultrasonic motion sensor, 1000 lux, USB-C power, a wireless dial, curved monitor support from 1000R to 1800R and 19.7W.

It ranks fifth because it is the front-light version of the Halo 2: the same dial and sensor without the backlight. It is a better desk light than RGB models.

Best for a clean desk glow. The caveat is no rear lighting.
pros: Motion sensor auto on and off

products.name: Quntis Curved RGB Monitor Light Bar, Dual Head Foldable
products.verdict: A foldable dual-head mount for 1000R to 1800R curved monitors.
products.description:
This Quntis is a foldable dual-head bar made for 1000R to 1800R curved monitors, with 15 RGB backlight modes, a remote and CRI 98 plus for screens of 34 inches and up.

It ranks sixth because the foldable heads keep it from sliding on a curved bezel, which flat mounts struggle with. It gives both front and RGB rear light.

Best for curved ultrawides. The caveat is that it suits larger screens.

products.name: Quntis RGB Pro+ Monitor Light Bar, 20-inch, 15 RGB Modes
products.verdict: A 20 inch bar with 15 RGB modes, 144 LEDs and a wireless remote.
products.description:
This Quntis RGB Pro+ is 20 inches long with 15 RGB backlight modes, a wireless remote, 144 LEDs, CRI 95 and four color temperatures.

It ranks seventh because it adds RGB to the long Quntis format, but the effects are simpler than Govee's sync.

Best for ultrawides with RGB. The caveat is simple effects.

products.name: Quntis Computer Monitor Lamp, 900 Lux, Touch Control
products.verdict: 900 lux with an auto-dimming sensor and CRI 98 at a low price.
products.description:
This Quntis lamp lists 900 lux, an auto-dimming sensor, touch control, CRI 98 and USB power, with no screen glare.

It ranks eighth because it is the plainest, with no remote, RGB or backlight. It is the cheapest way to light a desk.

Best for a budget desk light. The caveat is it is a lamp, not a gaming light.

products.name: Quntis Monitor Light Bar, 15.7-inch, 24 RGB Backlight Modes
products.verdict: A 15.7 inch bar with 24 RGB modes and 900 lux front light.
products.description:
This Quntis bar is 15.7 inches with 24 RGB backlight modes, a 900 lux front light, touch control, CRI 95 and USB power.

It ranks last because it is the shortest, so it suits smaller monitors best. It is the cheapest way to get RGB.

Best for a small gaming monitor. The caveat is the shorter length.

whatMatters.detail: A front light puts glare-free light on your desk. A backlight glows on the wall behind the screen and reduces contrast in a dark room. Decide which problem you have first.
A 15.7 inch bar suits a smaller screen, a 20 inch bar suits ultrawides. Check your monitor width.
Curved screens can cause flat mounts to slide. Look for a listed curvature range such as 1000R to 1800R.
Lux is brightness, from 900 to 1200 here. CRI is color accuracy, 95 to 98 on these listings. Higher helps keyboard and desk visibility.
A wireless dial or remote avoids reaching behind the monitor. Motion sensors turn the bar off for you.

faq.a: A soft light behind the screen that cuts the contrast between the panel and a dark wall. The BenQ Halo 2 and Razer Aether provide it.

faq.q: Will a light bar fit a curved monitor?
faq.a: Some do. The BenQ models list 1000R to 1800R and the Quntis Curved RGB is built for them.
It is a measure of brightness. The Quntis PRO+ lists 1200 lux.
For full effects on Govee and Razer, yes. BenQ and Quntis use a dial or remote.

faq.q: Does a light bar cause screen glare?
faq.a: Well-designed bars aim light at the desk, not the screen. The Quntis lamp lists no screen glare.
The 20 inch Quntis PRO+ and RGB Pro+ cover ultrawides.

finalTake: For most gamers, the BenQ ScreenBar Halo 2 is the right buy: front and back lighting with a wireless dial. For bright desk light on an ultrawide, take the Quntis PRO+. For screen sync, choose the Govee G1. For Razer setups, the Aether integrates with Chroma.
